items.stem: In Bayesian analysis, a conjugate prior is one for which:

options.text: The posterior is in the same family as the prior
options.rationale: Correct: conjugacy means prior and posterior share the same distributional family.
Conjugate priors need not be uniform.
The likelihood is always combined with the prior.
The posterior family depends on the conjugate pairing, not always normal.

items.explanation: Correct: conjugacy means prior and posterior share the same distributional family.

items.stem: A random-effects (mixed) model is preferred over a fixed-effects model when:

options.text: Groups are a random sample from a larger population and we want to generalize
options.rationale: Correct: random effects model group-level variation drawn from a population.

options.text: There is exactly one observation total
options.rationale: A single observation cannot support a mixed model.

options.text: All predictors are identical across observations
options.rationale: Identical predictors give no variation to model.
A constant response has nothing to explain.

items.explanation: Correct: random effects model group-level variation drawn from a population.

items.stem: Select TWO statements that correctly describe simulation (Monte Carlo) methods.

options.text: They approximate quantities of interest using many random draws
options.rationale: Correct: Monte Carlo estimates quantities from repeated random sampling.

options.text: Accuracy generally improves as the number of simulations grows
options.rationale: Correct: Monte Carlo error typically shrinks with more draws.

options.text: They always give the exact closed-form answer
options.rationale: Simulation gives approximations, not exact closed forms.

options.text: They require no random number generation
options.rationale: Random draws are fundamental to Monte Carlo.

options.text: They only work for normally distributed data
options.rationale: Monte Carlo applies to many distributions.

items.explanation: Correct: Monte Carlo estimates quantities from repeated random sampling.
